display.purpose: Page titles on public/marketing pages. Reserved for high-impact, single-line use.

body.purpose: Running text, descriptions, form help text. The readable voice of the interface.

label.purpose: Chips, tags, status badges, table column headers, metadata. The data voice.

shadows.name: popover
shadows.purpose: Menus, popovers, command palette. Light enough to read as floating without drama.

shadows.name: dialog
shadows.purpose: Modal dialogs and sheets. Heavier to establish the overlay relationship.

motion.name: transition-normal
motion.purpose: Standard state transitions, input focus, hover effects.

motion.name: transition-slow
motion.purpose: Panel reveals, layout shifts, larger element transitions.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Default action button. Command Charcoal fill, tight dimensions, 1px press feedback.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; height: 32px; padding: 0 10px; background: oklch(14.7% 0.004 49.25); color: oklch(98.5% 0.001 106.423); border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 6px; font-family: 'Source Serif 4', serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: background 120ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1), transform 120ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: oklch(14.7% 0.004 49.25 / 0.8); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(66.6% 0.179 58.318); outline-offset: 2px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px oklch(66.6% 0.179 58.318 / 0.24); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action button. Transparent with border, darkens on hover.

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard form input. Transparent background, Parade Line border, amber focus ring.
components.css: .ds-input { display: block; width: 100%; height: 32px; padding: 4px 10px; background: transparent; color: oklch(14.7% 0.004 49.25); border: 1px solid oklch(92.3% 0.003 48.717); border-radius: 6px; font-family: 'Source Serif 4', serif; font-size: 0.875rem; transition: border-color 120ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1), box-shadow 120ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1); outline: none; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: oklch(44.4% 0.011 73.639); } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: oklch(66.6% 0.179 58.318); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px oklch(66.6% 0.179 58.318 / 0.5); }

components.name: Card
components.description: Container surface. Formation Ivory background, 1px border, no shadow. Flat by rule.
components.css: .ds-card { background: oklch(98.5% 0.001 106.423); color: oklch(14.7% 0.004 49.25); border: 1px solid oklch(92.3% 0.003 48.717); border-radius: 4px; } .ds-card-header { padding: 24px 24px 0; font-family: 'Barlow Condensed', sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.2; } .ds-card-content { padding: 16px 24px 24px; font-family: 'Source Serif 4', serif; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.5; }

narrative.overview:
TroopToTask looks like the best briefing room you've ever walked into: clean sight lines, information-dense displays, everything exactly where you expect it. No decoration for its own sake. Every pixel either communicates status or enables action.

The system is restrained by conviction, not by timidity. Color is deployed with purpose: warm amber marks what needs attention, red marks what's wrong, and the rest stays out of the way. Typography pairs a condensed military-grade heading face with a legible serif body, reinforced by monospace for data and labels. The effect is authoritative without being cold, dense without being cluttered.

This is not consumer software dressed up in olive drab. It does not borrow startup aesthetics (pastel gradients, playful illustrations, bouncy micro-interactions) or repeat the mistakes of legacy military systems (green-on-gray brutalism, 12px system fonts, modal-driven workflows). It occupies its own lane: modern professional tooling built for people who manage formations, not features.
keyCharacteristics: Restrained color palette with a single warm accent
Tight radii and flat surfaces; depth comes from borders and background tints, not shadows
Condensed headings for density; serif body for sustained reading; mono for data
Transitions are fast and purposeful (120-240ms, exponential ease-out)
Information density is a feature, not a problem to solve

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Ops Amber is the only saturated color in the interface outside of status indicators. Its rarity is the point. If more than 10% of a screen surface is amber, reduce usage until it reads as signal, not decoration.

rules.name: The Tinted Neutral Rule
rules.body: Every neutral in the palette carries a warm hue tint (chroma 0.001-0.011, hue 48-106). Never use pure gray, #000, or #fff. The warmth is subtle but essential to the system's cohesion.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Every text element uses exactly one of the three font families. Barlow Condensed for structure. Source Serif 4 for content. IBM Plex Mono for data. Mixing within a single element is forbidden.

rules.name: The Flat Formation Rule
rules.body: If an element is in the page flow, it is flat. Shadows are exclusively for elements that break the page plane (popovers, dialogs, dropdowns). A card with a shadow is a bug.

dos: Do use OKLCH for all color definitions. Every neutral carries a warm hue tint (chroma 0.001-0.011). Verify with the Tinted Neutral Rule before adding any new color.
Do use the three-font system consistently: Barlow Condensed for structure, Source Serif 4 for content, IBM Plex Mono for data. No exceptions.
Do keep all transitions between 120-240ms using cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1). The three speed tokens cover every case.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion with the existing media query that collapses all animation durations to near-zero.
Do use tinted-background treatments for status colors (Alert Red at 10-20%, Readiness Green at 14%, Intel Blue at 14%). Solid saturated fills are reserved for chart elements only.
Do cap body text line length at 65-75ch.
donts: Don't use pastel gradients, playful illustrations, or bouncy animations. This is not consumer SaaS. If it could belong on a Notion or Linear marketing page, it does not belong here.
Don't use green-on-gray color schemes, 12px system fonts, or modal-first workflows. This is not legacy military software (DTMS, DTS, or any .mil system from 2004).
Don't add shadows to in-flow elements. Cards, buttons, inputs, table rows: all flat. If you're reaching for box-shadow on something that isn't a popover or dialog, stop.
Don't use #000, #fff, or any achromatic neutral. Every value must carry the warm tint.
Don't introduce a second accent color. The One Accent Rule: Ops Amber only. Status colors (red, green, blue) serve functional roles, not decorative ones.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on any element.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient background).
Don't use glassmorphism (blur + transparency as decoration).
Don't build hero-metric templates (big number, small label, gradient accent). Dense fact grids are fine; SaaS dashboard cliches are not.
